quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai annual report: 2025 Annual Report (03-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results (annual report): revenue RMB 4,823,405,697.64, up 32.07%; net profit attributable to shareholders RMB 263,485,209.59, up 58.08%; net profit excluding non-recurring items RMB 258,785,427.31, up 71.09%; operating cash flow RMB -470,648,364.60 (RMB 561,969,224.76 in 2024), which the company attributes to higher purchasing. Quarterly revenue: Q1 RMB 893,554,813.08, Q2 RMB 1,141,571,454.86, Q3 RMB 1,324,801,878.72, Q4 RMB 1,463,477,550.98; quarterly net profit attributable: Q1 RMB 31,433,649.67, Q2 RMB 89,470,756.88, Q3 RMB 138,388,632.85, Q4 RMB 4,192,170.19. The company reports an exchange loss of RMB 8,462 ten-thousand in 2025 (a gain of RMB 1,444 ten-thousand in 2024), about 32.11% of net profit, mainly because Hong Kong listing proceeds were held in Hong Kong dollars as the US and Hong Kong dollars fell.

quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai annual report: 2025 Annual Report (03-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Segments (annual report): high-speed optical module revenue RMB 1,675,383,015.45 in 2025, up 240.85%, gross margin 34.49% (up 10.27 percentage points); telecom broadband RMB 1,992,407,158.65, down 1.98%, gross margin 14.01% (down 4.78 points); wireless networking and edge computing RMB 1,153,962,178.57, up 2.51%, gross margin 19.00%. High-speed optical modules: output 899,963 units (+197.99%), sales 911,160 units (+156.11%), year-end inventory 148,567 units (-7.01%). Broadband shipped nearly 1,000 ten-thousand units for revenue of nearly RMB 20 hundred-million, with 10G PON over 50% of shipments and 25G PON shipping in volume to North American customers. Overseas revenue RMB 4,528,140,426.78, up 33.99%; overseas sales were 93.91% of revenue in 2025 (92.59% in 2024).
quarterly_data.figure: high-speed optical modules RMB 1,675,383,015.45 (+240.85%), gross margin 34.49%; module sales 911,160 units (+156.11%)

quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai annual report: 2025 Annual Report (03-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Products (annual report): in 2025 the company completed development and validation of its second-generation silicon-photonics 800G series, and the full silicon-photonics 800G series shipped in volume to overseas core customers; silicon-photonics 400G QSFP112 DR4/DR4+ and 800G OSFP DR8/DR8+ passed certification at large overseas customers and shipped in large volumes in 2025, and the new 800G OSFP 2xFR4/2xLR4 silicon-photonics products had largely completed certification at several large overseas customers ahead of large-volume shipments in 2026. The overseas R&D team developed and validated 1.6T OSFP DR8 and 1.6T OSFP 2xFR4 based on a 3nm DSP and 200G/lane high-density silicon photonics and sent customer samples in Q4 2025; in the domestic market 1.6T completed sample development with small-batch shipments. ELSFP external light sources and 3.2T NPO/CPO development started, with customer samples expected in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T OSFP (3nm DSP, 200G/lane) customer samples Q4 2025; 3.2T NPO/CPO samples expected 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai annual report: 2025 Annual Report (03-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capacity (annual report): the optical module lines moved from Shanghai to the new Jiashan (Zhejiang) factory, which passed a key North American customer's certification in July 2025 and reached over 90% of design capacity in November; the Malaysia base passed North American 400G and 800G module audits and ships in volume, and its broadband and wireless output doubled to 400 ten-thousand units; the company built more than 500 self-developed precision coupling machines; products exported to the US are mostly made in Malaysia, and the US factory completed first-phase trial production and certification. The company states that despite the large rise in 800G/1.6T capacity, its high-end capacity still has a phased gap against explosive AI data-center demand, and mass-production processes for CPO and 3.2T are still being verified. The Jiashan optoelectronic manufacturing base buildings (budget RMB 24,282.50 ten-thousand) are 100% complete, with RMB 246,776,455.16 transferred to fixed assets; construction in progress rose 101.28% to RMB 457,643,424.22, mainly Zhejiang plant equipment.
quarterly_data.figure: Jiashan over 90% of design capacity in November 2025; Malaysia broadband and wireless output 400 ten-thousand units

quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai annual report: 2025 Annual Report (03-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain (annual report): during the 800G ramp the company resolved shortages of laser chips, DSP chips and key passive optical components through executive-level supplier mechanisms and strategic agreements locking in core resources, and placed early orders for several key materials to lock capacity; prepayments rose 591.70% to RMB 168,639,509.56 and inventory rose 40.95% to RMB 2,375,753,927.22, mainly raw materials. For 2026 the company plans capacity-reservation agreements with leading global vendors for scarce 3nm DSPs and high-power lasers and expects tight raw-material supply to continue.

quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai annual report: 2025 Annual Report (03-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2026 business plan (annual report, company plan): optical modules focus on 1.6T mass production, more 800G capacity and next-generation technology - develop 1.6T DR8, 2xFR4 and the matching LPO / LRO versions, bring 1.6T OSFP DR8/DR8+ and 1.6T OSFP 2xFR4 into production with mass production and customer certification of the 3nm-DSP 1.6T silicon-photonics modules, continue ELSFP and 3.2T/6.4T/7.2T NPO/CPO development and start 3.2T OSFP module development; build new cleanrooms at Jiashan to expand module capacity substantially; a leased 8.88 ten-thousand square-metre plant near Jiashan had its first floor fitted out in March and enters production once customer audits pass; the Malaysia base is to finish COB, assembly-test and SMT workshop expansion in Q1, complete 800G new-product introduction, customer audits and volume shipment in H1 and start 1.6T trial production; North American capacity is to be built with Dallas as the operations centre and nearshore Mexico module production.
quarterly_data.figure: Malaysia: workshop expansion Q1 2026, 1.6T trial production 2026; leased plant 8.88 ten-thousand square metres
